subject: Seller-led pricing experiments and buyer entitlement path
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Bcc: 
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Seller-led pricing experiments + buyer entitlement path

Team —

Quick note as we prep the Acme Cloud private offer: procurement asked for a few different commit/term options and is explicit about buyer approval windows. I want to do a short seller-led experiment to see which structure reduces buyer friction while preserving ARR. Proposed matrix (attached):

- Option A: 12-month commit, usage overage allowed, 15% discount vs list; buyer approval: procurement + finance signoff
- Option B: 24-month commit, fixed annual invoice, 22% discount, requires procurement + CIO approval
- Option C: 3-month pilot (usage-based), then auto-roll to 12m at market price with a one-time onboarding credit; requires only procurement

Questions for you all:
1) Vanessa — what's the fastest path to register both A & B as separate SKUs/offers in AWS so we can generate two private-offer links? Any limits on overlapping offers for the same customer?
2) Karthik — from legal/PSA perspective, do we have standard clause templates to avoid long redlines for the longer-term (B) option?
3) Grace — can CS commit to a condensed onboarding for pilots so we can advertise <2 week time-to-first-value for Option C?

If the answers are quick, I'd like to go live with the experiment this week and send parallel private-offer links to Bethany at Acme. If we can, let's also request a quick procurement timeline from them so we can coordinate buyer approval gating (who signs at what commit level).

Attaching the spreadsheet with revenue model and suggested pricing bands.

Thanks —
Marcus
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing-experiments-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), po-approval-matrix.pdf (reference matrix)

> Quick note as we prep the Acme Cloud private offer: procurement asked for a few different commit/term options and is explicit about buyer approval windows. I want to do a short seller-led experiment to see which structure reduces buyer friction while preserving ARR. Proposed matrix (attached):
> 
> - Option A: 12-month commit, usage overage allowed, 15% discount vs list; buyer approval: procurement + finance signoff
> - Option B: 24-month commit, fixed annual invoice, 22% discount, requires procurement + CIO approval
> - Option C: 3-month pilot (usage-based), then auto-roll to 12m at market price with a one-time onboarding credit; requires only procurement

Marcus — good framing. Quick answers inline:

1) On AWS offer creation: we can create separate private offers for A and B (two offers pointing to same product id) without issue. The limitation is you cannot attach two concurrent private-offer IDs with identical pricing/term to the same buyer identity — but different SKUs/price listings are fine. I recommend publishing A and B under distinct price dimensions so we can track conversion separately.

2) For overlapping offers: AWS will accept parallel offers; they show up as separate entitlements on the buyer side. We should ensure the public product page reflects the canonical list price to avoid buyer confusion.

3) I will open a request with AWS Marketplace Seller Support to pre-validate the long-term offer flow and check whether buyer approval routing (procurement vs exec signature) affects the private offer acceptance UI. I'll loop them in if needed.

I can help generate the two private-offer links once legal gives us a greenlight on standard clauses.

—Vanessa
Director, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

Marcus / team —

Thanks for the rundown. A few legal/ops notes:

- Option B (24-month fixed) will likely trigger our legal to request an exceptions package for auto-renewal/termination language if we include early termination fees. If we keep renewal opt-in (no auto-charge) we reduce friction but lose some revenue stickiness.
- We have a short-form amendment for AWS marketplace private offers that limits redlines: parity on support SLAs, data handling aligned to our SOC 2 controls, and a clause for private-offer SKU mapping. I attached the current boilerplate to this reply (paste below).
- For buyer approvals: if the buyer requires CIO signature for > $500k ARR, suggest we route to a co-sell motion — loop in the field AE and ask for an exec intro so procurement can escalate. Otherwise procurement + finance is standard and can close in the marketplace without additional signatures.

Boilerplate (summary): support SLA = standard 99.5% uptime, liability cap = fees paid in 12 months, data residency = customer-managed keys supported.

I'll pre-clear the amendment with legal today and send a redline-friendly version.

-Karthik
Counsel, Commercial Contracts

Hi Marcus / team —

Thanks for the clear options. Procurement prefers Option C pilot-first for speed — they can get internal procurement approval within ~5 business days and would then route to finance if we convert. For the 24-month (Option B), our CIO generally signs anything above our multi-year threshold (roughly $400k/yr) so that aligns with Karthik's note.

A couple asks from Acme:
- Can you provide the private-offer links for Option A and Option C first (we want to pilot and compare 12m vs Pilot conversion)?
- For Option C, please confirm the onboarding credit is applied as a line-item credit on invoice and include a short statement in the DocuSign that the credit applies only on conversion to an annual commit within 90 days.
- Please share the short-form amendment Karthik mentioned so our legal team can do a quick review.

If you can send A + C by EOD Monday (our procurement meeting is Tue), we can move quickly.

Best —
Bethany Collins
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Cloud
